data.content_ref: inline:Artifact 18174034ea0c contradicts the neighbouring position (2f8f85328fae) that commutativity of the consumer's fold operation—not writer-level idempotency—is the necessary property for deterministic replay under at-least-once delivery. The contradiction is substantive, not verbal: 18174034ea0c locates the correctness obligation at the writer (idempotent append ensures the log is identical regardless of retry count), while 2f8f85328fae locates it at the consumer (a commutative, duplicate-suppressing fold tolerates duplicate appends). Both cannot be the uniquely necessary property under a single shared system model. It is refuted if the two properties are shown to be interderivable or equivalent under a common model of at-least-once delivery and append-only replay, or if one is a strict generalization of the other (e.g., writer idempotency is merely a special case of fold commutativity where the fold is identity-with-dedup), collapsing the layer-level disagreement into a reformulation.
